learning.why: Teacher ne PIL ko chitthi ke example se samjhaya aur bataya ki koi aur bhi file kar sakta hai, yeh sunkar thoda idea aaya ki garib log bhi justice le sakte hain.

Teacher ne PIL ka example diya aur bataya ki bina paise bhi court ja sakte hain, isse misconception thoda kam hua ki sirf ameer log hi court ja sakte hain, par abhi bhi free legal aid ke baare mein doubt hai.

end.summary:
• Reviewed the court structure: District Courts → High Courts → Supreme Court, with appeal as a possible further review.
• Practised distinguishing civil cases (deposit, inheritance) from criminal cases (theft, force, crime against society).
• Identified judicial review as checking laws against the Constitution and Fundamental Rights.
• Discussed PIL and free legal aid; understanding of access to justice and judicial independence remained incomplete.
end.parentNote: Vihaan practised the court hierarchy, appeals, civil and criminal cases, judicial review, PIL and free legal aid. They used case examples to classify disputes and later identified that PIL can be filed for people who need help. There was still a mix-up about whether people without money can access court services and how free legal aid works; it was not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask Vihaan to make a three-column chart for PIL, Lok Adalat and free legal aid, with one example of each.
